reason: The kernel implements the A&S 7.1.26 erf approximation in Triton with FP32 arithmetic. The only correctness hypothesis (c1: truncated coefficients might violate the contract's fixed 1e-6 absolute tolerance somewhere in the domain) was tested exhaustively: probe t6 swept all 65536 FP16 bit patterns (every finite legal input, including signed zeros, subnormals, and ±65504) through kernel.run on GPU and compared against FP64 erf rounded to FP32. Max absolute error was 4.172e-07 (at x=1.0) with 0 violations of the 1e-6 tolerance. Since the input domain is finite and fully enumerated, this is a complete correctness proof over the contract's entire declared domain; run() also returns a fresh FP32 tensor on x.device and preserves the input. Verdict: trust.
